description.narrative:
Stakeholder effects Improved access to affordable housing finance: Rapid urbanization in India and the lack of affordable housing finance has led to several challenges including congestion, pressure on basic amenities and a severe shortage of housing units in cities, especially in low-cost segment. As per an RBI report as of September-2019, the housing shortage in India is estimated to increase to 100 million housing units by 2022, and out of this 95 percent of shortage is from Low Income Groups (LIG) and Economically Weaker Section (EWS), segments with the remaining 5 percent of the shortage coming from Middle Income Groups (MIG) or above.
Market Impact - Competitiveness: IFC's support for the Project, will promote greater competitiveness in the affordable housing segment, by demonstrating the viability of providing such financing to lower income segments like EWS and LIS. The housing market in India is very active with both banks as well as NBFCs and housing finance companies (HFCs) engaging in providing housing finance. However, most banks as well as the larger NBFCs and HFCs focus on providing housing finance to higher income groups, and lower income groups remain unserved/underserved despite the massive shortages of affordable housing for these groups. Although IFC has been supporting the development of affordable housing financiers through continued interventions, the shortage is substantial and would require continuous support, including supporting the development of small finance banks and medium-sized regional NBFCs and HFCs that service lower-income groups.

The proposed project envisages a debt investment (in the form of an IFC A Loan) of up US$100 million (in USD or in Indian Rupee equivalent of the USD amount) in AU Small Finance Bank Limited (AUSFB or the Bank). The investment will be for a tenor of up to 7 years. AUSFB will use the proceeds of the investment to grow its business of providing affordable housing loans for the purchase/construction and extension of houses to individuals in India (the Project).
